title: Model Changelog (Customer-Facing) — Known Gaps, FAQs, and Workarounds (Support Playbook)
author: Dev Patel
body:
## Purpose
This page is a support-facing reference for the **customer-visible Model Changelog** feature (Console + docs + API surfaces). It documents early limitations, common customer questions, and approved support messaging.

Use this page when:
- A customer reports “model behavior changed without notice.”
- A customer requests an **immutable/auditable** release note stream (RSS/JSON/API).
- A customer sees a **missing, delayed, or confusing** changelog entry.
- An enterprise asks how changelog publication relates to **pinned versions**, rollouts, or change-management.

## Quick summary (what to tell customers)
- Redwood is standardizing model/version metadata and generating **customer-visible release notes** from a canonical source.
- The changelog is **version-scoped** (per model version) and designed to support **pinning, rollouts, and audits**.
- Some gaps are expected during the migration period (see “Known gaps”).

Approved one-liner:
> “We’re rolling out a consistent, versioned model changelog across Console/docs/API. During the migration, some historical notes and a small subset of changes may not yet be reflected; we can confirm the exact resolved model version and provide interim change context while entries are backfilled.”

## Current rollout state (Support view)
**Availability:** Limited beta (Console feature flag + docs feed). Not all accounts see it yet.

**Where customers may see it:**
- Console: Model page → **Changelog** tab (if enabled)
- Docs: Model release notes section (per-model landing pages)
- API/SDK: Some routes expose **resolved model_version** and a **changelog_url** (where enabled)

**What is authoritative right now:**
1) Resolved model version returned by the API/SDK (when present)
2) Published changelog entry for that exact model version
3) Internal model registry change-event + audit log (internal verification)

## Known gaps and limitations (expected)
### 1) Missing historical entries (pre-migration)
**Symptom:** Customers search for older model updates and see little or nothing prior to the migration window.

**Cause:** We did not have a single canonical changelog process historically; older updates lived in scattered channels (docs, ad-hoc messages, runtime notes).

**Support guidance / workaround:**
- Confirm the customer’s **time range** and **model_id/version_id**.
- Offer a **manual summary**: “We can provide what we know about major changes during that timeframe and confirm whether any serving/runtime changes were involved.”
- If the customer needs a formal record for audit/compliance, open an escalation (template below) so Release Eng can determine what can be backfilled or documented.

**Approved phrasing:**
> “We’re backfilling key historical notes where we have reliable provenance. For earlier periods, we can confirm your resolved version history and provide an interim written summary for your change-management records.”

### 2) Delayed publication (generator runs on a batch cadence)
**Symptom:** Customer hears about a rollout or notices a difference; the changelog entry appears later.

**Cause:** v1 supports batch publication (daily/controlled), plus an approval workflow (draft → in_review → published). Some entries wait on review.

**Support guidance / workaround:**
- Confirm whether the change is still **in_review** (internal status) vs actually missing.
- Provide the customer an ETA window when possible (same business day vs next day), without promising exact times.
- If customer impact is high, follow the “Urgent publish path” escalation.

**Approved phrasing:**
> “Release notes are published after validation and review, so there can be a short delay. I can confirm the resolved version you’re hitting right now and share an interim summary while the note is finalized.”

### 3) Not all change types are customer-visible in v1
**Symptom:** A customer expects low-level details (kernel swaps, exact hardware changes, vendor/model onboarding specifics) and doesn’t see them.

**Cause:** Customer-safe templates intentionally exclude internal-only details and sensitive operational metadata.

**Support guidance / workaround:**
- Focus on customer outcomes: compatibility, observable behavior changes, supported features, deprecation timelines.
- For enterprise: offer a structured response aligned to their questionnaire (what changed, when, impact, rollback plan) without leaking restricted info.

**Approved phrasing:**
> “We publish customer-relevant impacts (compatibility, behavior/quality notes at a high level, deprecations, and links to relevant metrics). We intentionally exclude internal operational details, but we can discuss the impact and mitigations for your workload.”

### 4) Changelog may not explain “quality differences” beyond links/metrics
**Symptom:** Customer wants a narrative like “why did it become more verbose” or “why did tool calling break.”

**Cause:** v1 does not generate deep natural-language narratives from eval diffs. It may include links/metrics and short summaries.

**Support guidance / workaround:**
- Ask for a minimal reproducible prompt set and expected outputs.
- Confirm pinning and compare resolved versions.
- If needed, route to Applied ML / Model Catalog for evaluation-based analysis.

### 5) Multiple changes in a short window can be confusing
**Symptom:** Customer sees multiple entries on the same day or thinks “the changelog changed.”

**Cause:** Metadata edits, corrections, and rollouts can occur close together. Corrections are handled via a **superseding entry** (history preserved).

**Support guidance / workaround:**
- Explain the correction model: “superseded” vs “edited in place.”
- Point customer to the latest published entry and note prior entry IDs remain in history for audit.

**Approved phrasing:**
> “If an entry needs correction, we publish a new superseding note rather than rewriting history. That preserves an auditable trail while ensuring the latest guidance is clear.”

### 6) Console/docs link mismatch or 404 (staging and early rollouts)
**Symptom:** Console changelog link opens a 404, or docs don’t show the entry yet.

**Cause:** Docs publish job lag, caching/ETag issues, or environment mismatch.

**Support guidance / workaround:**
- Ask if the issue is in **staging vs production**.
- Provide the entry text (internal view) if customer is blocked.
- File an internal helpdesk ticket if it’s an environment/publish pipeline issue.

## FAQs (Support answers)
### Q1: “We pinned the model version. Why did outputs change?”
**Triage checklist:**
1) Confirm what the customer pinned (model name vs explicit version).
2) Confirm the **resolved model_version** returned in responses (if available).
3) Check whether a **runtime release** or serving configuration change could affect outputs/latency.
4) Ask for a specific request_id / timestamps / region.

**Support response (template):**
> “Let’s verify the exact resolved model version and serving path for the requests you’re referencing. If the resolved version is unchanged, we’ll check for runtime/serving changes that could affect behavior, and we’ll document findings and mitigations.”

### Q2: “Do you provide an RSS/Atom or JSON feed of model changes?”
**Current answer:**
- RSS/Atom + JSON feed exists/rolling out, but may be gated by rollout stage.
- For accounts without access: offer interim email notification + manual export (where available).

**Support response (template):**
> “Yes—there’s a machine-readable feed for published model release notes. If it’s not enabled for your account yet, we can provide an interim notification path and flag you for early access.”

### Q3: “Is the changelog immutable/auditable for enterprise change-management?”
**Current answer:**
- Customer-visible notes are published via an approval workflow.
- Corrections are superseded (history preserved).
- Internal audit events record actor/timestamp/event identifiers.

**Support response (template):**
> “Published entries are versioned and we preserve a history when corrections are required. Internally, changes and publish actions generate audit events with actor and timestamp. For your security review, we can share our retention and audit approach at a high level and align on the evidence you need.”

### Q4: “Will I get notified before a deprecation/sunset?”
**Current answer:**
- Deprecations include a sunset date and replacement guidance (when applicable).
- Timing follows the model version change-management policy; enterprise accounts can request longer notice.

**Support response (template):**
> “Deprecations are announced with a sunset timeline and recommended replacement. If you have a formal change window, we can coordinate on notice periods and rollout controls.”

### Q5: “Can you customize release notes per account / per region?”
**Current answer:**
- Not in v1. Notes are global per model version.
- Workaround: support can provide account-specific impact guidance if the customer shares their usage pattern.

## Troubleshooting playbook (step-by-step)
### Step 1 — Collect minimum details
Request:
- model name and (if possible) pinned version
- environment (Hosted/Dedicated/Private) and region
- timestamps and request_ids
- what changed (behavior/latency/errors/tool calling/structured outputs)
- whether Console changelog is visible + link if present

### Step 2 — Determine whether this is (a) missing note, (b) delayed note, or (c) wrong note
- Missing note: no published entry exists for the version.
- Delayed note: internal draft/in_review exists.
- Wrong note: customer claims the published note is inaccurate/confusing.

### Step 3 — Provide customer with a stable reference
- Best: send the **changelog URL** for the exact version.
- Otherwise: quote the customer-safe summary and include “effective date” and “version id.”

### Step 4 — If customer impact is active, recommend immediate mitigations
Depending on scenario:
- Pin to a prior version (if available/allowed) and document the pin.
- Pause/slow rollout (Dedicated/Private) via rollout controls.
- Route to fallback model variant if configured.

### Step 5 — Escalate with the right tags
Use the escalation templates below.

## Escalation templates
### A) Missing/Delayed changelog entry (Support → Release Engineering)
**Subject:** Missing/Delayed model changelog entry for <model_id> <version_id> impacting customer

Include:
- customer/account: <name>
- impact: <prod issue / change mgmt blocker / procurement>
- model_id/version_id and region
- observed date/time window
- whether rollout is active
- requested ETA and required wording constraints (if enterprise)

### B) Correction request (confusing or inaccurate customer-visible wording)
**Subject:** Changelog correction requested for <model_id> <version_id> — customer report

Include:
- link to published entry
- what’s confusing/incorrect (quote exact lines)
- proposed corrected wording (customer-safe)
- whether we need a same-day hotfix publish

### C) Enterprise audit/immutability questionnaire
**Subject:** Enterprise request: auditable model release notes / retention expectations

Include:
- questionnaire items (paste)
- required formats (RSS/JSON/API export)
- retention expectations (e.g., 1/3/7 years)
- who is requesting (security/procurement/engineering)

## Do / Don’t for Support messaging
### Do
- Confirm resolved model_version and date range.
- Use “customer-impact” language: compatibility, feature support, deprecations, mitigations.
- Offer interim summaries when notes are missing/delayed.
- Be explicit about migration limitations and expected improvements.

### Don’t
- Don’t share internal model nicknames, vendor-specific procurement details, or internal-only metadata fields.
- Don’t promise exact publish timestamps.
- Don’t imply the changelog is complete for all history yet.

## Customer-safe snippets (copy/paste)
1) Migration gap
> “We’re in the process of migrating historical model updates into a consistent, versioned changelog. Some older entries may not appear yet, but we can confirm the exact version you’re on and provide interim context for your records.”

2) Approval delay
> “Release notes go through validation and a review step before publication, so there can be a brief delay. I can share the resolved version and impact summary now, and I’ll follow up as soon as the entry is published.”

3) Correction/supersede
> “If we ever need to correct an entry, we publish a superseding note rather than rewriting history. That keeps an auditable trail while ensuring the latest guidance is clear.”
